encoding.frame: Requests and responses are [type: uint8][payload length: uint32][payload]. A request's type is its command id, a response's its response id. Each request gets exactly one response, in order.

fieldTypes.bool: 1 byte: 0 is false, 1 is true (readers take any non-zero byte as true).
fieldTypes.string: A uint32 byte count, then that many bytes of UTF-8, with no terminator.
fieldTypes.json: Identical to string on the wire: a uint32 byte count, then UTF-8 JSON text. Written json (any JSON value) or json:<shape>, where a shape is string, number, bool, json (any value), a jsonTypes entry, or a shape followed by []. A jsonTypes entry maps each key to a shape; a key ending in ? is optional. Clients with codecs parse the text; to anything else it is a string.
fieldTypes.bytes: The rest of the payload, with no length prefix. Only ever the last field.
fieldTypes.mat4: 16 float32, column-major (element col * 4 + row) for column vectors, so the translation is elements 12, 13 and 14.
fieldTypes.<type>: An entry of types: its fields in order, with no prefix.
fieldTypes.<type>[]: Elements of <type> back to back, with no length prefix: their number is the uint32 field named count declared before the array.

encoding.errorPayload: An Error response's payload is the message as raw UTF-8 bytes, not a string: the frame's length is the message's byte count.
encoding.reservedIds: Ids 0xC0 to 0xFE are reserved for server-pushed event frames: no command or response uses them.
encoding.versioning: version is major.minor.patch. The minor version goes up for new commands, new responses, new trailing request fields and new trailing response fields; anything else (a changed id, field order or type, a removed field) bumps the major version. Both directions must keep working within a major version: a server reads a trailing request field only when the payload has bytes left and otherwise uses a default, since a client of an older minor version doesn't send it (Commands.hpp: ReadTrailing); a client's decoders ignore response bytes after the fields they know, and a client relies on a response field added in a later minor version only once Hello has shown the server speaks that version. Hello refuses a client whose major version differs from the server's, and accepts any minor version with a warning when it differs.

RenderFrame.description: Renders one frame at the viewport size (SetViewportSize; 1280x720 until it is called). pixels is width * height * 4 bytes of RGBA8, top row first, alpha 255, on every renderer backend, so it can be drawn as-is (e.g. as canvas ImageData).

SetViewportSize.description: Sets the size, in pixels, that later RenderFrame frames are rendered at (each 1 to 4096; anything else is an Error). The renderer itself is resized, so frames are neither cropped nor resampled, and the camera's aspect follows.

Hello.description: Opens a session: the client's name, the protocol version it speaks (its PROTOCOL_VERSION) and the host's access token (empty when it has none). Error when the major versions differ, or when the host requires a token and this isn't it. Optional on a host without a token. On a host with one, every other command (Shutdown included) is refused with an Error until a Hello on the same connection succeeds, and a failed Hello ends the session. The session belongs to the connection: a client that reconnects sends Hello again. capabilities names optional features beyond what the version implies (none are defined yet); projectLoaded is whether the host has a project (was started with --project).

PollEvents.description: Returns the server's events after afterSeq, oldest first: log lines (every line the host logs, from startup on) and, in later versions, other kinds. Seqs are numbered from 1 within an epoch, a random non-zero number the server picks when it starts (and again if seqs would pass 4294967295, when it starts over at 1). One rule: afterSeq means the last seq the client has seen in the epoch it passes; when that epoch is not 0 and is not the server's, or afterSeq is newer than any seq of the server's epoch, the server reads afterSeq as 0. So a client passes epoch 0 and afterSeq 0 first, then each response's epoch and nextSeq: reconnecting to the same host it misses nothing and gets nothing twice, and after the host restarted (or started over) it gets the new epoch's events from the start. Returns at most maxEvents (and at most 1024) events; nextSeq is the last one's seq, or, when none is returned, the newest seq, so maxEvents 0 skips everything retained. The server keeps the newest 4096 events (and about 2 MiB of them); dropped counts the events after afterSeq that fell off before this poll. A client polls it (about every 100 ms); it never logs, so an idle server returns no events. A log event is {seq, kind: "log", level: "info" | "warn" | "error", message, time: Unix milliseconds}. Since 1.3.0: sceneChanged {revision, savedRevision, path} whenever the scene revision moves, a scene is saved, or another is loaded (path is the loaded scene's file, empty for none). Since 1.4.0 it also says what changed: entityIds, the UUIDs of the objects whose GetEntity data the change touched (those it created, destroyed with everything under them, renamed, re-tagged or moved to another layer; and, with everything under them, those it reparented, transformed, activated or deactivated, whose world matrices or activeInHierarchy changed with them, and the copy and its subtree for a duplicate), when there are at most 256 of them. It doesn't list the siblings whose index shifted: header.index is only guaranteed fresh in a GetHierarchy read, so a client that shows the tree refetches it when the revision moves; full: true when another scene was loaded (OpenScene, NewScene, LoadScene), so every id a client holds is invalid and it refetches everything. A save changes no object and carries neither. Any other event with neither (a change that touched more than 256 objects) means anything may have changed, so a client refetches what it shows; one with entityIds lets it refetch only those, and GetHierarchy when the revision moved. assetsChanged {added, removed, modified} (res:// paths, each sorted) after a RescanAssets that found changes, and, since 1.9.0, after the host's file watcher found changes (it looks about once a second while a client is connected, so a file added, edited or deleted outside the editor is reported without a RescanAssets) and after WriteTextAsset, CreateScriptAsset and SetImportSettings (modified, though its file is the same, for the last); an asset of a kind the engine can reload that is held in memory is reloaded before the event is sent (see WriteTextAsset); projectChanged {} after project.n2proj was saved. historyChanged {canUndo, canRedo, label, redoLabel, undoCount, redoCount} since 1.6.0, after a step is recorded, undone or redone, or the history is cleared (label is the step Undo would undo, redoLabel the one Redo would redo, empty for none; the counts are the steps done and undone); an edit merged into the step before it (typing in a number box) sends none. Since 1.6.0 sceneChanged also follows Undo, Redo and RestoreAutosave, with full: true when the step was undone or redone by restoring a snapshot of the scene. Since 1.7.0: frameChanged {revision} when what the viewport would show has changed (the scene, the editor camera, the viewport size, the assets or the project's settings) since the last frame RenderFrameIfChanged rendered: one event per change that follows a rendered frame, not one per change, so dragging the camera sends one. revision is the revision the next frame will have (a later change before that frame moves it on); a client that is showing the viewport answers it with RenderFrameIfChanged. A client ignores kinds and keys it doesn't know.

RenderFrameIfChanged.description: Renders the editor view only when it changed, so an idle edit-mode viewport costs nothing. The editor view is the open scene drawn from the editor camera (SetEditorCamera) at the viewport size, whether or not the scene has a camera of its own, and without simulating. Every picture has a frame revision (a uint32, never 0): it moves on whenever the scene, the editor camera, the viewport size, the assets or the project's settings change. sinceRevision is the revision of the frame the client holds, or 0 for none. When it is the current revision, the answer is modified false, with the revision, the viewport size and no pixels (a few bytes, and no rendering). Otherwise it renders (or, if the frame of the current revision is still in the server's buffer, resends it) and answers modified true with the frame's revision, width, height and pixels, laid out as RenderFrame's. A client that wants a frame whatever the revision (it dropped its copy) passes 0. Polling it every animation frame is cheap; the frameChanged event (PollEvents) says when a poll will find a new frame. A revision means nothing across hosts (a host starts numbering at a random number), so a client that reconnects keeps its frame only when the revision it holds comes back as current. RenderFrame is unchanged and draws the game's main camera (SetCameraPosition moves it), as a play-mode viewport will; it neither uses nor moves the revision. Error when there is no renderer or it can't make the render target.

SetEditorCamera.description: Sets the editor camera, the viewpoint of RenderFrameIfChanged's frames. The server owns it: it isn't a scene object, isn't saved with a scene and isn't part of undo; the game's main camera (SetCameraPosition) is separate. The client computes orbit, pan, zoom and fly and sends the resulting pose. rotation is a quaternion (normalised on receipt; the camera looks down its local -Z, +Y is up). fovY is the perspective camera's vertical field of view in degrees (1 to 179). With orthographic true the camera is orthographic: orthoSize is its half height in world units (0.0001 to 1000000) and the width follows the viewport's aspect ratio. nearPlane and farPlane are distances along the view direction: a perspective camera needs 0.0001 to 1000000 for the near plane, an orthographic one -1000000 to 1000000; the far plane must be at least 0.001 beyond the near plane and at most 10000000. Each position coordinate is within +-1000000. Every number must be a finite number: NaN and infinities are refused, never clamped, and a zero quaternion is refused; a refused request is an Error and changes nothing. Setting the camera it already has changes nothing (no new frame). Only the values of the projection in use are range-checked, so a client may keep an unused fovY or orthoSize at any finite value. Applied at once, so the next RenderFrameIfChanged shows it. Never logs (clients send it every frame while dragging).

GetEditorCamera.description: The editor camera as stored (position, the normalised rotation, fovY, orthographic, orthoSize, nearPlane, farPlane: SetEditorCamera's fields), and the view and projection matrices frames are rendered with at the current viewport size, so a client's gizmos and overlays line up with the picture. The matrices are mat4, for column vectors: view takes world to camera space (the camera looks down -Z) and projection camera space to clip space, so clip = projection * view * (world point, 1). The projection uses the viewport's aspect ratio, so it changes with SetViewportSize. A server that never had SetEditorCamera answers with the defaults: position (0, 0, 10), no rotation, a 60 degree perspective camera, near 0.1, far 1000, orthoSize 5. Never logs.

PickEntity.description: The object under a point of the editor view, for clicking in the viewport (since 1.8.0). x and y are pixels in the viewport, the origin its top-left corner and y pointing down, as the frames RenderFrameIfChanged returns (SetViewportSize's size): a point outside the viewport (or a non-finite one: an Error) picks nothing. The server casts a ray through the point from the editor camera (SetEditorCamera) at the viewport size and tests it against the open scene's renderables on the CPU, with no physics (an edit-mode scene has no bodies, and most visual objects have no collider). Each active renderable with world bounds is a candidate, tried nearest box first and then exactly: the triangles of a mesh (MeshRenderer and the built-in cube, sphere and quad, either face), the laid-out text rectangle of a TextRenderer, and for a world-space canvas the topmost graphic under the ray (any graphic, whatever its raycast target; entityId is that graphic's object, and a ray through an empty part of the canvas goes on to what is behind). An object with a transform and no shape of its own (an empty object, a light, a camera, text with no text) is picked by a sphere of radius 0.25 world units around its position, but a UI object (a canvas, or anything with a RectTransform) never is; an object without a transform has no place in the world and is never picked. Screen-space overlay canvases are not part of the editor view and are never picked. The nearest hit between the camera's near and far planes wins; at the same distance, the object earlier in hierarchy order. includeInactive false skips objects that are inactive (in the hierarchy) and disabled components; true picks them too (a canvas's graphics follow its layout, which skips inactive objects either way). entityId is the object's UUID string, empty for a miss (then point is (0, 0, 0) and distance 0); point is where the ray meets it in world space; distance is the length from the ray's origin, the point on the camera's near plane under the pixel, to point, in world units. Pure: it changes nothing and never logs (clients send it on every click or mouse move).

GetEntityBounds.description: World-space bounds of objects, for "frame selected" and a selection box (since 1.8.0). entityIds is a JSON array of object UUID strings (at most 4096; anything else is an Error). bounds has one {id, min, max} for each of them that has bounds, in the order asked (an id asked twice is answered once); min and max are the corners of an axis-aligned box in world space. An id that names no object is left out, not an Error, as is an object with neither a transform nor any bounds below it, so a client compares what it asked with what came back. An object's box is the union of the world bounds of the renderables on it and on everything under it (a rotated mesh's box is larger than the mesh: it is a box around the transformed mesh bounds), plus the rect of each UI element of a world-space canvas; descendants that are switched off don't count (nor what is under them), nor does a disabled renderable component, and the object itself counts even when it is inactive; a UI element of an inactive object or canvas has no rect to measure. An object with nothing to measure but a transform (an empty object, a light; not a UI object, which has only its rect) gets the box of its pick sphere: 0.25 world units either side of its position, so "frame selected" has something to frame. Pure: it changes nothing and never logs. Error when there is no scene.

DeleteScene.description: Deprecated: scene files are .scene assets under assets/ now (OpenScene, SaveSceneToFile). Deletes <project>/scenes/<sceneName>.json, the scene folder of the protocol before projects; never the loaded scene's.

OpenScene.description: Opens a scene file of the project: reads it, builds it in edit mode (no component is attached) and makes it the loaded scene, replacing the loaded one (unsaved changes are lost: a client asks first). A scene path is res:// then a path inside the project's assets folder ending in .scene (any case); anything else is an Error. Error without a project, for a missing file, or for one that isn't a valid scene; the loaded scene is kept then. The scene's uuid is its file's asset UUID, the same every run. revision is the scene revision, which every command that changes the loaded scene or loads another moves on (it only grows); savedRevision is the revision the scene was last opened or saved at, so the scene has unsaved changes exactly when revision != savedRevision. Opening moves the revision on and counts as a save.

SaveSceneToFile.description: Writes the loaded scene to a file of the project (its JSON, indented, replacing the file atomically) and stores it in the host as SaveScene does. path empty: the scene's own file (an Error when it has none); another path saves it there (overwriting a file that exists), which becomes the scene's file and gives it that file's uuid. A scene path is res:// then a path inside the project's assets folder ending in .scene (any case); anything else is an Error. savedRevision becomes revision.

NewScene.description: Makes an empty scene the loaded scene, named name (empty: the file's name without .scene, or Untitled). With a path, the scene is written there first, and an existing file is an Error (open it instead); with an empty path it has no file (path is empty) until SaveSceneToFile names one. A scene path is res:// then a path inside the project's assets folder ending in .scene (any case); anything else is an Error. It starts saved: revision equals savedRevision.

GetHierarchy.description: The loaded scene's objects as one flat list in depth-first order (a parent before its children, siblings in their order): each node is {id, parentId (empty for a root of the scene), index (its place among its siblings), name, active (its own flag), activeInHierarchy (it and every ancestor are active), layer, tag, components (the type names, in order)}. revision is the scene revision the list was read at: a client refetches the list when a sceneChanged event's revision moves past the one it holds. Error when no scene is loaded.

GetOpenScene.description: The loaded scene: its file (path, empty when it has none), name, uuid, revision and savedRevision. Error when no scene is loaded. A host started with --project always has one: its startup scene, or an empty one with no file.

CreateEntityEx.description: Makes a GameObject in the loaded scene, with a transform (CreateEntity's has none) and what preset adds: empty or Empty (nothing), Cube, Sphere or Quad (the renderer of that name), Light or DirectionalLight, PointLight, SpotLight (a Light of that type). An empty name is the preset's own (GameObject, Cube, Directional Light, ...). parentId empty makes it a root of the scene, anything else its parent; siblingIndex is its place among its siblings, -1 (or past the last) meaning the last. Error, with nothing made, without a scene, for a parent that isn't in the scene, or for a preset it doesn't know.

SetEntityParent.description: Moves an object under another (parentId; empty makes it a root of the scene) at siblingIndex among its new siblings (-1, or past the last: the last). keepWorldTransform true keeps where the object is in the world (its local transform changes to match), false keeps its local transform (it moves with its new parent). Moving it to the place it already has changes nothing and doesn't move the revision. Error without a scene, for an object or a parent that isn't in the scene, and when the parent is the object itself or one of its descendants.

SetEntityProperties.description: Changes an object's own properties: properties is a JSON object with any of name (string), active (bool, the object's own flag), tag (string) and layer (integer, 0 to 31). A key it doesn't know, or a value of the wrong type or out of range, is an Error, and then nothing is changed. A property that already has the value changes nothing and doesn't move the revision. A scene the host opened for editing (every scene it loads) runs no OnEnable or OnDisable on the object's components when active changes: none of them was ever enabled.

DuplicateEntity.description: Copies an object and everything under it, placing the copy right after the original among its siblings (under the same parent) and naming it as Unity does: Cube gives Cube (1), then Cube (2), and Cube (1) is another copy of Cube. Every object and component of the copy has a new UUID. References between objects of the copy point at the copy; references to anything else in the scene are kept (they still point at the same objects), and a reference to something that isn't in the scene comes back null. Answers the copy's id.

GetEntity.description: One object in full. entity is {header (id, parentId, index, name, active, activeInHierarchy, layer and tag, as a hierarchy node has them), transform (the local position, rotation and scale, rotation a quaternion; absent for an object that has no transform), components (each {type, uuid, values}: values is the component's saved form, what Scene saves for it, in component order)}. worldMatrix is the object's local-to-world matrix (the identity for an object with no transform), so a client draws a gizmo without walking the parent chain. Error when there is no scene or no such object.

SetLocalTransform.description: Sets an object's transform relative to its parent (to the scene, for a root). rotation is a quaternion, so an inspector that shows Euler angles doesn't drift through round trips; the host normalises it, and a zero quaternion (or one too large to normalise) is an Error. An object that has no transform (CreateEntity makes such objects) gets one. Setting the transform an object already has changes nothing and doesn't move the revision. Error for a value that isn't a finite number, and without a scene or an object.

RescanAssets.description: Indexes the project's assets again: new and changed files get .meta files, and deleted files are forgotten (they no longer load by path or UUID; their .meta files are kept, so import settings come back with the file). When anything changed, an assetsChanged event lists it: {added, removed, modified}, res:// paths, each sorted. Since 1.9.0 the host does this by itself about once a second while a client is connected (see PollEvents's assetsChanged), so a client needs this command only to force a scan, and a script or other asset held in memory whose file changed is reloaded here as the watcher does (see WriteTextAsset).

ListAssets.description: The assets in a folder of the project (since 1.9.0): the files the engine indexes (those whose extension has a loader: scripts, textures, fonts, audio, materials, models, scenes), each with its UUID, which is its .meta's. folder is a res:// path ("res://" or empty for the whole assets folder, "res://scenes"); it must be an existing folder, else an Error. A path is "res://" then a path inside the project's assets folder ("res://scripts/Player.lua"); a path with "..", a drive or root, a name Windows can't hold (a character of <>:"|?*, a control character, a name ending in a dot or space, a device name such as CON) or one that leaves the folder through a symbolic link is an Error. recursive false lists the folder's own files and subfolders, true everything below it. folders is a JSON array of the subfolders' res:// paths (without a trailing slash), found by walking the file system, because the metadata doesn't know empty folders (symbolic links to folders are left out); assets is a JSON array of AssetInfo: {path, uuid, type, size, modified, subAssets?}. type is the resource type ("LuaScript", "Texture", "Font", "AudioClip", "Material", "Model", "Scene"), size the file's bytes, modified its modification time in Unix milliseconds, both as the last scan saw them (the watcher scans about once a second while a client is connected, and an assetsChanged event follows a change). subAssets, only on a file that has them (a model's meshes, materials and textures), lists {key, uuid, type} for each, as the .meta's index recorded them when the model last loaded; a model never loaded has none yet. Both arrays are sorted by path; the answer isn't paged. Pure: it changes nothing and never logs. Error without a project.

GetAssetInfo.description: One asset's details (since 1.9.0). uuidOrPath is a res:// path (checked as in ListAssets) or the UUID string of an asset file. info is an AssetDetails: ListAssets's AssetInfo plus customData, the import settings from the asset's .meta (the sub-asset index the engine keeps there, customData.subAssets and subAssetsSource, is not part of it: it is subAssets), and loaded, whether the engine holds the asset in memory now. customData is {} for an asset with no settings, and SetImportSettings takes the same object back. Error for a path or UUID that is not an indexed asset (a sub-asset's UUID names a part of a file: ask for the file) and without a project. Pure: it never logs.

SetImportSettings.description: Replaces an asset's import settings, the customData of its .meta, and saves the .meta (since 1.9.0). customData must be a JSON object of at most 65536 bytes of JSON text (anything else is an Error), whatever shape the asset's loader reads (for example {"texture": {"filter": "nearest"}}); keys the loader doesn't know are kept. The keys subAssets and subAssetsSource are the engine's own index of a model's parts: they are left as they are, and the same keys in customData are ignored. The change is a replacement, not a merge: GetAssetInfo, change, send back. When the engine holds the asset in memory it is dropped, so the next use loads it with the new settings (objects already holding the old copy keep it until they are rebuilt), the viewport's frame revision moves on, and an assetsChanged event lists the path as modified. Error for a path that is not an indexed asset, and without a project.

ReadTextAsset.description: Reads a text file of the project (since 1.9.0), for the script editor. path is a res:// path to an existing file whose extension is one of .lua, .mat, .scene, .json, .txt, .md, .csv, .xml, .yaml, .yml, .toml, .ini, .cfg, .glsl, .vert, .frag, .shader (any case); another extension is an Error, so a binary asset is never sent as text. The file must be at most 4194304 bytes and valid UTF-8 (a byte order mark is kept: it is part of the text), else an Error. text is the file's content as it is, line endings included. Pure: it never logs. Error without a project.

WriteTextAsset.description: Writes a text file of the project (since 1.9.0), creating it when it doesn't exist (its folder must: see CreateFolder). path as in ReadTextAsset, text at most 4194304 bytes of valid UTF-8 without NUL characters, else an Error; it is written as it is (no line ending is added or changed), through a temporary file renamed over the old one, so a crash or a full disk never leaves half a file. A path that names the open scene's file is an Error (the scene in memory would differ from the file: use SaveSceneToFile). Afterwards the file is indexed, or its .meta brought up to date, and an assetsChanged event lists it as added or modified. When the engine holds a script (.lua) in memory it is reloaded at once: its new source is read, its module runs again and the LuaComponents using it rebuild their script instances (their saved fields carry over), as the watcher does for a change made outside the editor. A script that fails to load or run is not an Error of this command: the error is logged (a log event) and the write stays. Any other asset held in memory is dropped, so the next use loads the new file. Error without a project. There is no undo for a file write.

CreateScriptAsset.description: Creates a Lua behaviour script from the engine's template (since 1.9.0), replacing the client-side write of CreateScript's template. path is a res:// path ending in .lua (any case) that doesn't exist yet (an Error if it does); the folders above it that are missing are created. className is the name the script's class gets, made into a valid Lua identifier as CreateScript's name is ("my enemy" becomes "My_enemy"); empty uses the file's name. The file is written atomically and indexed (an assetsChanged event lists it as added). path is the file's path as the file system spells it and uuid its asset UUID. Error without a project.

CreateFolder.description: Creates a folder under the assets folder, and the folders above it that are missing (since 1.9.0). path as in ListAssets, but not the assets folder itself. Ok when the folder already exists; an Error when a file is in the way. An empty folder is no asset, so no event follows (ListAssets finds it, as it walks the file system). Error without a project.

GetComponentTypes.description: Every component type the host can create, sorted by name, each as a ComponentSchema: its typeName, whether an object can have only one (singleton), its editable fields (FieldSchema: name, displayName, kind, typeName, hidden, readOnly, and when they apply enumOptions, assetType, min and max, tooltip, container), and defaults, the JSON a new component of the type saves (isActive included, the random uuid left out). The fields are what the type registered with RegisterMember and its relatives, so they are the keys the component saves besides uuid and isActive (a LuaComponent is the exception: its fields are scriptUUID and the current script's, which the types list can't know, see GetLuaFields; what it saves is scriptUUID or scriptPath, and scriptData). A field's kind decides its editor: Bool, Int, Float, String, Vector2, Vector3, Vector4 and Quaternion are objects of numbers ({x,y,z} and so on); Color is {r,g,b,a} when typeName is Color, or {x,y,z} (Vector3) or {w,x,y,z} (Vector4) for a vector marked as a colour (Light.color); Enum is a string, one of enumOptions; AssetRef and AssetRefList are a UUID string (an array of them) or null, of an asset whose type is assetType; GameObjectRef, GameObjectRefList, ComponentRef and ComponentRefList are a UUID string (an array of them) or null; Json is whatever the member's own JSON is, shown as a JSON editor. A field with a container is not at the top of the component's JSON but inside its object of that name (the script fields of a LuaComponent, in scriptData, with a reference written {"$ref": uuid}). The types never change while the host runs, so a client keeps the answer; ask again after Hello.

AddComponent.description: Adds a new component of the type typeName (a name from GetComponentTypes) to an object, with the values a new component has: componentId is its UUID and values its saved form (what GetComponent returns). Error for an unknown type, a singleton type the object already has, or without a scene or an object. The scene revision moves and sceneChanged lists the object.

RemoveComponent.description: Removes one component from an object, by the UUID GetEntity and AddComponent give (the second of two of a type, too). Error when the object has no such component. In a scene the host opened for editing the component never attached, so it gets no OnDisable or OnDestroy (a script's callbacks don't run), and every component reference to it in the scene is cleared. The scene revision moves and sceneChanged lists the object.

SetComponentFields.description: Sets fields of one component. values is a partial JSON object in the shape GetComponent returns: only the keys it has are touched (a field it doesn't mention keeps its value, a list included), isActive is accepted, and a field with a container is set as the container's key holding an object of just those fields. Keys that are not fields are refused, except an echo: the uuid, a LuaComponent's scriptPath, or the scriptData of one without a script, when it is what the component has, so what GetComponent returned can be sent back. A number a member's C++ type can't hold (an integer outside its range, a negative for an unsigned, a float beyond what a float holds) is refused. A LuaComponent's scriptUUID and scriptData are set in separate requests (the data is checked against the script the component has when the request arrives). The text is refused when it nests deeper than 64 levels or has more than 200000 values. It is all or nothing: every value is checked against its field (a wrong type, a name that isn't one of an enum's options, a reference that isn't a UUID or null, a UUID that names nothing in the scene or an asset of another type than the field's assetType, an unknown or read-only field) and applied to a copy first, and any problem is an Error naming the field with nothing changed. A field with a range is clamped. The response is the component's values as stored (clamped, enum names canonical), so a client shows what was kept. Setting values that are already stored changes nothing and doesn't move the revision; otherwise the revision moves, sceneChanged lists the object, and the component's OnEditorFieldsChanged runs with the keys that changed. Edit mode only in practice: a client doesn't send it to a play-mode host (the inspector is read-only while playing).

GetComponent.description: One component's values, as it saves them (the same JSON GetEntity lists under components, and Scene saves). Error when the object or the component isn't found.

GetLuaFields.description: The fields of one LuaComponent as its script declares them: a ComponentSchema (typeName LuaComponent, no defaults) whose fields are scriptUUID (an AssetRef to a LuaScript, so the script can be changed) and one per entry of the script's SerializableFields, with container scriptData. A script field's kind is its declared type (type = "string", "int", "number", "bool", "Vector3", "GameObject" or a component type name) or else what its default is (an integer is Int, another number Float, a boolean, a string, a Vector3); anything else is Json. The fields are sorted by name. A component without a loaded script has only scriptUUID. Error when the component isn't a LuaComponent.

GetProjectInfo.description: The project the host opened (--project): its folder and user:// folder (absolute paths, UTF-8) and its project.n2proj as saved, unknown keys included. Error without a project.

SetProjectSettings.description: Changes the project's settings with a JSON merge patch (RFC 7386: a key set to null is removed, objects merge, anything else replaces), applies the blocks it touches to the running engine (layers, input, physics) and saves project.n2proj. settings must be an object. When a subsystem refuses its block (or the file can't be saved), nothing is saved, the live state from before the patch is put back, and the Error names the blocks. Answers the project as saved. Error without a project.

SetStartupScene.description: Sets the scene a host opens first (project.n2proj's startupScene) and saves the project file. path is an existing scene file (res:// then a path inside the project's assets folder ending in .scene, any case), which is also added to the scene list, or empty for none; anything else is an Error. Answers the project as saved. Error without a project.

Undo.description: Undoes the step that was done last: the latest edit made by an editing command (CreateEntity, CreateEntityEx, DuplicateEntity, DestroyEntity, SetEntityTransform, SetLocalTransform, SetEntityParent, SetEntityProperties, AddComponent, RemoveComponent, SetComponentFields) or, when it was made between BeginEditGroup and EndEditGroup, the whole group. Answers EditResult: the step's label, the scene revision after it, whether another step can be undone or redone, and savedRevision. Error without a scene, with nothing to undo, or while a group is open (end it first); a step that can't be undone (an object it needs is gone) clears the history and the Error says so. The revision moves and sceneChanged follows: entityIds names the objects the step touched, or full is true when the step was undone by putting back a snapshot of the scene (undoing DestroyEntity, RemoveComponent or RestoreAutosave rebuilds every object, with the same UUIDs), so a client refetches everything. Undoing back to the state the scene was last opened or saved at makes savedRevision equal the revision (no unsaved changes). historyChanged follows. Editing commands are meant for a scene opened for editing: a client doesn't send them to a play-mode host.

Redo.description: Redoes the step Undo undid last; the same answer and errors as Undo, for redoing. A new edit after an Undo discards what could have been redone.

BeginEditGroup.description: Starts a group: every edit until the matching EndEditGroup becomes one undo step labelled label (a gizmo drag, a paste of several fields). Edits of the same thing in a group (the same object's transform, the same component's same fields) are kept as one, so a drag holds one before and one after however many requests it sends. Groups nest: an inner group is part of the outer one, which gives the label, up to 16 deep (Error past that). Undo and Redo are refused while a group is open. A group left open when its client disconnects, or by a new Hello, is ended by the host; opening, creating or loading another scene discards it. label is cut to 100 bytes.

EndEditGroup.description: Ends the innermost group opened by BeginEditGroup; ending the outermost makes its edits one step (none when it held no edit). Error when no group is open. historyChanged follows a step, and so does the autosave (see GetAutosave).

GetHistory.description: The undo history, for an Edit menu: entries is every step, oldest first, each {label, bytes} (bytes is what the step holds in memory), and cursor is how many of them are done: entries before it can be undone (the last of them is what Undo undoes), the rest redone. The history holds at most 200 steps and 128 MiB (the newest step is always kept) and drops the oldest first; it is kept when the scene is saved and cleared when a scene is opened, created or loaded.

GetAutosave.description: Whether the host holds an autosave of the open scene, and where: info is {exists, and when it does: path (the file, absolute), size (bytes), modified (Unix milliseconds)}. The host writes the autosave to <project>/.n2/autosave/ (the scene's path under assets/, or .untitled.scene for a scene with no file) when an edit step ends while the scene has unsaved changes (at most once per 2 seconds; the last one is written by the host's loop), and removes it when the scene is saved or is back at its saved state. It never writes the scene's own file. An autosave found when a scene is opened is kept and not overwritten until RestoreAutosave, DiscardAutosave or a save, so a client that finds one after a crash can offer it. Error without a project or a scene.

RestoreAutosave.description: Replaces the open scene's content with its autosave, as one undoable step labelled "Restore autosave" (the scene then has unsaved changes, and every object is rebuilt with the UUIDs the autosave has: a sceneChanged with full follows). Answers the open scene as OpenScene does. Error without a project or a scene, without an autosave, or when it isn't a valid scene (it is kept then).

DiscardAutosave.description: Deletes the open scene's autosave (and lets the host write new ones). Ok when there was none. Error without a project or a scene.
